messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

message.content:
At a pressure of roughly 10 kPa (about 0.1 atm) water’s freezing point drops to **≈ –2 °C**.  
This is because the solid–liquid equilibrium line for water bends toward lower temperatures as pressure falls below atmospheric pressure. At 10 kPa the equilibrium temperature is just below 0 °C, giving a freezing point of about –2 °C.
